verdict.rationale: Homebrew's docs and community evidence confirm a large, actively maintained ecosystem: formulae, casks, taps for third-party repos, bottling for fast binary installs, and cross-platform (macOS/Linux/WSL) support, with users explicitly praising the breadth of available packages ('brew had and has many more packages available') and quick version updates. Some community friction exists around tap-hosting difficulty and packaging complexity for niche software, but this doesn't contradict the core claim of broad, maintained package availability. Missing for 10: independent package-count statistics or third-party benchmarks comparing registry size/freshness against other package managers.
